# Import Contractual Limits

Contractual limits can be manually entered from the Master Characteristics screen\* or from a tab-delimited file (contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="InlineLink">Customer Support</a> to obtain the file format).

\* This method requires the **Master Characteristics** module.

The import process supports the import of data for a single meter or multiple meters in the same file.

Contractual limits belong to a specified meter and are <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">datetime effective<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Datetime effective records have a defined start date and time and a defined end date and time.</span></a>. Meters are not auto-created during the contractual limit import process, so the meters associated with the data must exist in FLOWCAL prior to importing a file.

<div class="procedure">

To import a contractual limits file:

1.  Go to **Import** \> **Contractual Limits**.
2.  Click the browse button next to the Import File field to select the import file (example: C:\data\ContractualLimits.txt), or type the file path in the field.
3.  Click the **Import** button. The process bar next to the Import button will display the percentage of the file completed as it is processed. Any errors generated during the import process will be displayed in the messages window.
4.  Go to **Setup**\> **Meter** \> **Master Data Validation** to view the imported data.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 410;height: 370;" />

Contractual limits can be entered or imported manually. The file import service does not support the import of contractual limits.

</div>

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.
